initiative.name: Launch U.S.–Philippines Instant Remittance
initiative.description: A digital payment service allowing eligible U.S. customers to send money to recipients in the Philippines.
initiative.businessJustification: Provide a faster, lower-friction remittance experience for existing U.S. customers while expanding the bank's digital payments offering.

businessContext.targetCustomers: Existing U.S.-domiciled consumer customers who pass onboarding and transaction eligibility checks.
businessContext.paymentFlow: U.S. customer funds transfer from a bank account or debit card; FULCRUM demo partner routes funds to an eligible Philippine recipient account or wallet.
knownGaps: Confirm partner beneficial ownership and sanctions-screening evidence
Confirm alert-handling SLA and escalation ownership

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: Initial business proposal submitted for FCRM review.

comments.author: Daniel Reyes
comments.text: Partner ownership and alert escalation evidence remain open.

riskFactors.statement: Cross-border remittance and rapid movement of funds may increase layering and mule-account exposure.
International transfer capability creates exposure requiring recipient, purpose, and transaction monitoring controls.
The cross-border flow and partner payout network require robust screening and escalation evidence.
New digital channel and instant settlement increase account-takeover, stolen-funding, and social-engineering exposure.
Destination-country and corridor exposure requires documented geographic-risk treatment.
Existing U.S. customers are in scope, but recipient information and beneficial-purpose context may be incomplete.
Instant remittance combines digital onboarding, cross-border payment, and rapid payout in a new service.
Expected volume and velocity require tuned monitoring, limits, and escalation capacity.
Mobile/web self-service and non-face-to-face initiation increase identity and fraud-control dependency.
A new local payout partner creates dependency on partner diligence, screening, monitoring, and issue escalation.
Core KYC and sanctions controls exist, but partner due diligence and enhanced monitoring evidence are incomplete.

controls.name: Customer identity verification and KYC
controls.mitigation: Reduces unidentified-customer exposure but does not eliminate fraud or misuse.

controls.name: Sanctions screening at customer and transaction stages
controls.mitigation: Reduces screening exposure; partner and escalation evidence remains incomplete.

controls.name: Transaction monitoring and velocity alerting
controls.mitigation: Reduces suspicious-activity exposure; enhanced remittance rules are still being implemented.

controls.name: Third-party due diligence and ongoing oversight
controls.mitigation: Reduces partner risk; beneficial ownership and periodic review evidence is incomplete.

controls.name: Fraud detection, step-up authentication, and limits
controls.mitigation: Reduces digital fraud exposure; launch limits and tuning are conditions of approval.

facts: Screening control operating with partner dependency

aiObservations.statement: AI recommends HIGH residual risk because partner due diligence and enhanced monitoring evidence are incomplete.
Confirm recipient wallet limits and partner alert escalation ownership before launch.

overrides.rationale: The initial AI recommendation treated all partner evidence gaps as uncontrolled. The analyst accepted the documented KYC/screening controls and the bounded initial launch scope, while retaining conditions for the remaining gaps.
downstreamImpact: Committee package retained HIGH system-calculated residual risk
Conditions created for enhanced monitoring and partner diligence

analystRecommendation.rationale: Proceed only with bounded launch controls and explicit conditions; system-calculated residual risk remains HIGH until conditions are verified.

votes.comment: Approve bounded launch subject to the listed conditions and post-launch review.

finalDecision.rationale: The committee accepts the bounded launch risk with conditions that address monitoring, limits, partner diligence, and post-launch oversight.

conditions.description: Implement enhanced transaction monitoring rules RM-01–RM-05 and evidence alert-handling ownership.
Maintain lower initial transaction limits until 30-day monitoring review is completed.
Complete additional due diligence on HarborBridge, including beneficial ownership and escalation SLA evidence.
Perform a 30-day post-launch FCRM review of corridor, customer, transaction, fraud, and sanctions alerts.
